Tomato_Early_Blight.name: Tomato Early Blight
symptoms: Concentric ring spots ('target board' pattern) on older leaves
Yellowing surrounding leaf spots
Lower leaves drop prematurely
Dark sunken spots on stems near ground level
organic_remedies: Apply Neem oil spray every 7-10 days
Spray copper fungicide or bio-fungicide (Bacillus subtilis)
Mulch soil around plants to prevent fungal spores from splashing up
Prune lower infected leaves to improve air circulation
chemical_treatments: Azoxystrobin or Difenoconazole systemic fungicide for active outbreak
preventive_measures: Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous plants
Use drip irrigation instead of overhead watering
Plant resistant tomato varieties (e.g., Mountain Magic, Defiant)

Tomato_Late_Blight.name: Tomato Late Blight
symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked dark lesions on leaves and stems
White fungal fuzzy growth on underside of leaves in humid conditions
Rapid wilting and browning of entire foliage
Brown firm rot on tomato fruits
organic_remedies: Apply copper sulfate or Bordeaux mixture immediately at first sign
Remove and destroy severely infected plants immediately (do not compost)
Maintain strict canopy airflow and dry foliage
preventive_measures: Destroy volunteer tomato and potato plants nearby
Avoid planting near potato fields
Apply preventive bio-fungicide prior to wet cool weather

Tomato_Bacterial_Spot.name: Tomato Bacterial Spot
symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots with yellow halos on leaves
Leaf spots turn brown and foliage appears shot-through
Scab-like rough raised spots on fruits
organic_remedies: Fixed copper mixed with mancozeb or bio-bactericide
Streptomyces lydicus biological fungicide
preventive_measures: Use certified disease-free seeds
Avoid handling wet plants
Sterilize garden tools with 70% isopropyl alcohol

Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.name: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (TYLCV)
symptoms: Severe stunting of young tomato plants
Upward curling and yellowing of leaf margins
Leaves become leathery and thick
Flowers drop before fruiting
organic_remedies: Control Whitefly vector using yellow sticky traps
Spray Insecticidal soap or Neem oil regularly to kill whiteflies
Cover crops with fine insect netting (mesh size < 0.6mm)
chemical_treatments: Imidacloprid or Thiamethoxam systemic insecticide for whitefly control
preventive_measures: Plant TYLCV-resistant hybrids (e.g., Tycoon, Inbar)
Reflective silver mulches to repel whiteflies

Tomato_Healthy.name: Tomato Healthy Leaf
symptoms: Vibrant deep green foliage
No spots, lesions, or discoloration
Firm, upright stem and vigorous growth
organic_remedies: No disease treatment required!
Maintain regular balanced organic fertilization (Compost, Kelp meal)
chemical_treatments: None needed. Keep up standard care.
preventive_measures: Maintain consistent watering schedule
Provide 6-8 hours of direct sunlight daily
Monitor foliage weekly for early pest detection

Potato_Early_Blight.name: Potato Early Blight
symptoms: Target-like dark brown spots on mature leaves
Yellowing surrounding leaf lesions
Tuber surface shows dark, leathery, sunken spots
organic_remedies: Copper octanoate spray
Bacillus subtilis foliage application
preventive_measures: Ensure proper plant nitrogen fertilization
Avoid leaf wetness during early morning/evening

Potato_Late_Blight.name: Potato Late Blight
symptoms: Dark water-soaked leaf spots rapidly enlarging
White powdery growth on leaf undersides during high humidity
Tubers rot in soil with reddish-brown dry rot
organic_remedies: Copper hydroxide spray at 5-day intervals during wet weather
Immediate destruction of infected vines before harvest
preventive_measures: Plant certified seed potatoes only
Hill soil well over tubers to protect from falling spores

Corn_Common_Rust.name: Corn Common Rust
symptoms: Golden-brown to cinnamon-red pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces
Pustules rupture releasing powdery rust spores
Severe infection causes leaf chlorosis and premature drying
organic_remedies: Sulfur-based organic fungicide spray
Neem oil spray
preventive_measures: Plant rust-resistant corn hybrids
Early planting to avoid peak spore migration

Apple_Scab.name: Apple Scab
symptoms: Olive-green to velvety brown spots on leaf surfaces
Leaves become distorted, yellow, and drop early
Dark corky scab lesions on apple fruit
organic_remedies: Liquid lime-sulfur or copper soap spray at bud break
Rake and burn fallen leaf litter in autumn to destroy overwintering fungi
preventive_measures: Prune tree canopy for maximum sunlight and airflow
Choose scab-resistant apple cultivars (e.g., Liberty, Enterprise)

Healthy_Leaf.name: Healthy Plant Leaf
symptoms: Clean leaf blade with uniform coloration
No fungal lesions, rust, or bacterial spots
Turgid and vigorous cellular structure
organic_remedies: No disease remedies needed!
Maintain soil health with organic compost and compost tea
preventive_measures: Provide optimal sunlight, nutrients, and moisture
Inspect plants regularly for early detection
